title: Partial push of a version leaves it unrepairable
notes: On a tag run, publish.sh pushes X.Y.Z first, then X.Y.Z-fixtures and the main tags. If a later push fails (network, quota), a rerun finds X.Y.Z already exists and fails by design, so the release can never get its -fixtures tag; the only way out is a new version. Pushing the -fixtures tag and the main tags before the bare version tag would shorten the window. Closed at the pivot: Rule 17: says nothing a viewer or operator would notice (a test's strength, a refactor, tooling or an internal cost). Reopen with the effect someone sees and its evidence.
